items.gist: The passage uses the metaphor of nourishing a seed with rasa to describe how the ritual act fills and strengthens the saṃvid-devī.
Viśveśvara Bodhabhairava is worshipped by those seeking bhoga or mokṣa, while even devotees of other deities are directed toward non-dual awareness.
Other deities are created, vidhi-dependent beings, whereas the I-awareness of consciousness is eternal and self-manifesting.
Those who sink into objecthood remain limited, but those who rest in consciousness attain the unbounded Lord.
The word 'I' everywhere denotes consciousness alone; the sacrificer is consciousness, not any external deity-form.
The self becomes covered and enters inert states, yet its covered and uncovered forms display a striking duality.
The Lord's freedom is unlimited; veiling varies by grade, and detailed treatment is deferred to śaktipāta.
The Lord reveals his full form partially to different knowers, producing varied grades of knowledge.
The means of knowledge is itself knowledge, subtle and will-like; kriyāśakti is the single cause of bondage and liberation.
Direct will-like awareness is icchopāya, repeated conceptual reflection is jñānopāya, and external ritual action is kriyopāya.
Kriyā is ultimately knowledge itself; yoga and liberation consist in the manifestation of one's own nature.
Liberation is not other than self-manifestation; powers are not non-conscious, and svātantrya resolves into śaktis.
Liberation is not an inevitable effect of knowledge, so the objection that knowledge would not liberate does not apply.
Action is knowledge in a coarser form; differences among upāyas do not imply differences in liberation.
The threefold samāveśa is taught in the śāstra, beginning with the śāmbhava type.
Śāmbhava, śākta, and āṇava samāveśas are distinguished by absence, mental, and ritual-imaginative means.
The śāmbhava samāveśa arises suddenly through the guru's superior awakening, without conceptual effort.
Samāveśa through consciousness is identity with Śiva, not merely an instrumental means, and later determinations follow from grace.
